claims.statement: The projectivized Example B.1 arrangement has exactly five bounded regions.
For the Figure 16 source-vector boundary under the pinned counterclockwise labeling, the divisor-filtered numerical replay produces five critical-point witnesses.
limitations: The boundary coordinates are rounded from PDF vector paths to one micro-point.
The five roots are floating-point witnesses.
The boundary labeling is canonicalized by an explicit anchor and orientation but is not sourced from printed boundary labels.
Genericity, interval isolation, and exact quotient dimension remain uncertified.

claims.statement: Each retained Figure 16 boundary witness passes the encoded numerical divisor, residual, orthogonality, adjacent-minor, and winding checks.
limitations: The checks use floating-point arithmetic and are not interval certified.

claims.statement: The five planar patterns embedded as vector paths in Figure 16 have been extracted into deterministic face-coordinate records and rendered from those records.
limitations: This is a replication of source vector geometry, not an independent reconstruction from the master-function witnesses.
Kawasaki conditions are checked only to PDF illustration precision.

claims.statement: The reduced bipartite topology inferred from Figure 16 admits the pinned positive weight representative, whose almost-perfect-matching boundary measurement reproduces the support and all nineteen nonzero Plucker coordinates of C up to one common scale.
limitations: The positive weights are numerical rather than exact symbolic values.
The weight-recovery optimization is not yet independently reproduced in the governed package.
The replay enumerates thirty-one almost-perfect matchings and obtains a maximum relative minor residual below 1e-12.

claims.statement: Extending the five algebraic witnesses through the reconstructed weighted graph and integrating their Kenyon-Smirnov primitives yields five distinct numerical planar t-embeddings with the prescribed boundary.
limitations: The roots and graph weights are floating-point inputs.
The discrete-holomorphic systems use numerical normal equations.
The result is an independent numerical reconstruction of five t-embeddings, not an exact formal proof.

claims.statement: The five independently generated numerical t-embeddings have been matched bijectively to the five source-vector drawings modulo a declared geometric equivalence group.
claims.blocker: A permutation-and-equivalence matcher between generated coordinates and the rounded source drawings has not been admitted.

claims.statement: A retained algebraic or planar solution is continuously rigidly deployable, collision-free, finite-thickness, or manufacturable.
claims.interpretation: Refuted only as an inference from the current evidence; no downstream physical conclusion follows from WP00.
